description: Configuration for a Potato annotation task. Generated from the live schema and display registries — see potato/server_utils/config_schema.py.

annotation_routing.description: Route high-confidence predictions past the annotator instead of asking

bald_params.description: Ensemble size and bootstrap fraction for `query_strategy: bald`

calibrate_probabilities.description: Calibrate the fitted model's probabilities, and keep the calibration only when it measurably helps

classifier.description: The model that scores unlabeled items. `{name: ...}`, optionally with `hyperparameters`. `name` takes a short name (`logistic`, `random_forest`, `svm`) or a fully qualified import path such as `sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression`

classifier_params.description: Extra keyword arguments passed to the classifier constructor

cold_start_strategy.description: How items are ordered before the first fit: random or llm

confidence_method.description: How an LLM's confidence is read: logprobs, verbalized or consistency

database.description: Ignored. Run history is recorded through the project database and needs no configuration

enabled.description: Turn active learning on. Also set `assignment_strategy: active_learning`, or nothing reorders

hybrid_weights.description: Weights for `query_strategy: hybrid`. Must sum to 1.0

icl_ensemble_params.description: How the ICL weight decays as real annotations accumulate

llm.description: Use a model rather than a classifier for cold start and confidence: `{enabled, endpoint_url, model_name}`

max_instances_to_reorder.description: Cap on how many unlabeled items are ranked per pass. They are sampled, not taken from the head of the file

min_annotations_per_instance.description: How many annotations an item needs before it can be training data

min_instances_for_training.description: How many labeled items must exist before the first fit. Below this the cold-start strategy decides the order

model_persistence.description: Save fitted models to disk: `{enabled, save_directory, retention_count}`

query_strategy.description: What "informative" means: uncertainty, diversity, badge, bald or hybrid

random_sample_percent.description: Fraction of each reordered batch left random, so the queue keeps exploring instead of only exploiting the model

resolution_strategy.description: How several annotators' labels become one training label: majority_vote, first, or unanimous

schema_names.description: Which schemes are learned. Defaults to every scheme with something learnable to predict

update_frequency.description: Retrain after this many new annotations

use_icl_ensemble.description: Blend in-context-learning predictions into the ranking

vectorizer.description: How items become features. `{name: ...}`, optionally with `hyperparameters`. `name` takes `tfidf`, `count` or `sentence-transformers`, or a fully qualified import path

vectorizer_params.description: Extra keyword arguments passed to the vectorizer constructor. A YAML list for `ngram_range` is coerced to the tuple sklearn wants

adjudication.description: Resolve disagreements through an adjudication queue

admin_api_key.description: Shared key for the admin API, sent as the X-API-Key header. Generated and persisted to {task_dir}/admin_api_key.txt when unset

agent_proxy.description: Run an agent as the subject of annotation

agreement_metrics.description: Which inter-annotator agreement measures the admin pages compute

ai_budget.description: Cost estimate and spend cap for AI actions. The complaint about commercial platforms is not the price but the surprise -- credits consumed by auto-labelling and discovered at export time

cap_usd.description: Dollar ceiling for this project's AI spend. A run projected to cross it is refused BEFORE it starts, so it cannot leave a part-labelled dataset and a bill for it

ai_support.description: Model-backed label suggestions shown alongside each item

ai_config.description: Everything about the model itself: model, base_url, api_key, max_tokens, temperature, timeout, include. One level deeper than the obvious guess — ai_support.model is not read

ai_config_file.description: Path to a separate YAML file holding the endpoint settings, so keys stay out of the repo. Its keys are merged FLAT into ai_config, so the file holds model/base_url/api_key directly — a nested ai_config: block inside it becomes ai_config.ai_config and is ignored. endpoint_type is the one key lifted to the ai_support level. A missing file disables AI support with a warning, which `validate --strict` treats as an error

cache_config.description: Disk cache and prefetch for model replies, so an annotator does not wait for a generation the study has already paid for

enabled.description: Turn AI assistance on. Without an endpoint that starts, the boot log says so and no assistant appears

endpoint_type.description: Which backend to talk to: openai, openai_vision, anthropic, anthropic_vision, gemini, huggingface, ollama, ollama_vision, openrouter, vllm, yolo, sam, sam3

image_key.description: Item field holding the image, when the item also carries text. Without it a vision endpoint only ever sees `item_properties.text_key`

alert_time_each_instance.description: Seconds an annotator may spend on one item before being warned. The default is effectively no limit

allow_phase_back_navigation.description: Let annotators go back to an earlier workflow phase. Off by default, so consent and training cannot be revisited and re-answered

analytics.description: Cost and latency analytics over ingested traces: optional per-model pricing, and the thresholds that raise a regression alert

pricing.description: Per-model token pricing used to turn token counts into money

thresholds.description: Fractional increases that trip an alert: cost_per_trace (0.5), avg_latency_ms (0.3), and error_rate as absolute percentage points (0.05)

annotation_codebook_url.description: Link to an external codebook, shown to annotators

annotation_instructions.description: Instructions shown on every annotation page, as inline text; a filename here renders as that filename

annotation_schemes.description: The annotation form. Each entry renders one widget.

annotation_type.description: Annotation type, as registered in the schema registry.

Dropdown selection

Free-form text input

Tool/resource-contention timeline: per-agent lanes + shared-resource collision classification

Per-step trajectory evaluation with error taxonomy and severity scoring

Video player display

Voice/full-duplex turn-taking: dual-track timeline + barge-in/overlap classification

annotation_task_description.description: Longer task description; falls back to task_description when absent

annotation_telemetry.description: The drawing-process analogue of keystroke_logging: content-blind telemetry on geometry schemas -- when someone draws, zooms, revises and accepts AI suggestions, never what or where -- and the rubber-stamping screening built on it

fidelity.description: How much is kept: off, summary (per-annotation statistics only), or events (raw streams as well)

flush_interval_ms.description: How often the browser posts its buffered events

idle_ms.description: Gap above which the annotator is charged to idle rather than active time. Two minutes rather than something tighter, because studying a hard image is real work that produces no events at all

include_schemas.description: Schemes to record. Empty means every geometry schema

store_events.description: Write raw event streams. Does nothing at summary fidelity

annotation_ui.description: Annotation-surface toggles that are not gated on QDA mode

memos.description: Show the memo sidebar. Unset means off in standard mode and on under qda_mode/solo_mode; set explicitly it wins either way

visibility.description: Visibility a new memo gets: private or shared. Anything else falls back to private

annotator_dashboard.description: Read-only progress page at /progress. Shows project totals and the requesting annotator's own stats, never another annotator's identity. A bare `true` is accepted as shorthand for `{enabled: true}`

show_active_annotators.description: Show how many annotators are currently active

show_personal_progress.description: Show the requesting annotator's own counts

arena.description: Multi-model arena: send one prompt to several providers and collect side-by-side preferences

models.description: Models to fan out to. Each is endpoint_type plus model, with optional label, base_url, temperature and ai_config

assignment_strategy.description: How items are handed out to annotators.

attention_checks.description: Insert items with a known answer to detect inattentive annotators

failure_handling.description: What to do when an annotator fails a check. A bare action name, or a mapping with warn/block thresholds and messages

frequency.description: Insert a check every N items

geometry_iou_tolerance.description: Overlap a drawn answer must reach to count as correct, as a fraction

min_response_time.description: Responses faster than this many seconds count as a failure

probability.description: Chance of inserting a check, as an alternative to frequency

audio_annotation.description: Server-side waveform service backing audio_annotation schemes. Only read when the task actually has one

client_fallback_max_duration.description: Seconds of audio the browser may decode itself when the server has no waveform ready

waveform_cache_dir.description: Where precomputed waveforms are cached. Relative paths resolve against task_dir; unset it is waveform_cache/ there

waveform_look_ahead.description: Clips whose waveforms are precomputed ahead of the annotator

authentication.description: Identity provider settings for SSO and database-backed accounts

allow_local_login.description: Keep username/password registration available alongside SSO

allowed_domains.description: Email domains permitted to sign in through SSO

allowed_org.description: Organization permitted to sign in through SSO

auto_register.description: Create an account the first time an SSO identity signs in

database_url.description: SQLAlchemy URL for the database backend; falls back to the POTATO_DB_CONNECTION environment variable

method.description: Which backend holds accounts: in_memory (the default), database, oauth or clerk

providers.description: OAuth provider settings, keyed by provider name

user_config_path.description: JSONL file of registered accounts, one {username, password} object per line, with the password stored as salt$hash. Under the default in_memory backend this is the ONLY thing that makes accounts survive a restart: unset, registrations live in memory and every annotator loses their login when the server stops, while their annotations remain in output_annotation_dir. Set it on anything an annotator will come back to

user_identity_field.description: Which claim from the identity provider becomes the Potato username

auto_redirect_delay.description: Milliseconds on the completion page before that redirect fires

auto_redirect_on_completion.description: Send annotators to the crowd platform's completion URL when they finish, instead of leaving them on the done page

automatic_assignment.description: Assign items to annotators automatically as they arrive

automation.description: Rules engine over incoming items: filter, sample, then act

rules.description: Rules of `when` (the shared condition grammar), an optional sample rate, and the actions to take on a match

batch_assignment.description: Split items into named groups and assign whole batches

boundary_probing.description: Boundary Lab. After a label is chosen, shows counterfactual edits of the item and asks whether they flip it -- which maps the decision boundary and exports as a contrast set

ai_support.description: Endpoint override for the llm tier; falls back to the global ai_support block

debounce_ms.description: Delay between choosing a label and fetching probes

include_invariance.description: Include a meaning-preserving paraphrase probe. A paraphrase that flips the label is the quality-control signal this exists to catch

precomputed_key.description: Item field holding precomputed counterfactuals, a list of `{text, kind: flip|invariance}`

probes_per_item.description: Probes per (instance, label), counting the invariance probe

rationale_on_flip.description: Ask for a short written reason when the annotator says a probe flips their label

schema.description: Scheme whose labels are probed. Defaults to the first radio scheme

sources.description: Ordered generation tiers -- precomputed, llm, rules. Earlier tiers win and later ones fill the remaining slots

bws_config.description: Best-worst scaling. Builds the tuples annotators compare and scores the results into a ranking. Its presence is what enables BWS

min_item_appearances.description: Times each item must appear across the tuples

num_tuples.description: Tuples generated in total, or null to derive the count from min_item_appearances

scoring.description: Scoring block; `method` selects the estimator (counting by default)

seed.description: Seed for tuple generation, so a design can be reproduced

calibration.description: Agreement drift tracking and the re-calibration prompt on /admin/iaa. Agreement is scored per time window so a fall in recent work is visible, instead of averaging into one whole-project number

drop_threshold.description: Relative fall below the project baseline that raises the re-calibration prompt, e.g. 0.15 for 15%

enabled.description: Compute the agreement timeline. Costs one extra IAA pass per window, so it can be turned off on very large projects

window_by.description: 'count' gives every window the same number of items, 'time' the same duration. Equal-count is the default because a study that ran in bursts leaves equal-duration windows empty, and an empty window has no agreement rather than low agreement

windows.description: How many time windows the timeline is cut into

cases.description: Group instances into units of analysis -- a participant, an interview -- so codes can be counted per case rather than per item

attributes.description: Item fields lifted onto the case so they can be crosstabbed

auto_detect.description: Scan loaded items for cases at startup. Set false to assign cases by hand

enabled.description: Turn case grouping on or off explicitly. Unset, it follows qda_mode

key.description: Item field to group on. Unset, detection scans participant_id, respondent_id and case_id

category_assignment.description: Route items to annotators by the item's category, optionally gated on a qualification the annotator earned in training

category_key.description: Item field holding the category. Must be a non-empty string

dynamic.description: Probabilistic expertise routing, which learns who is good at what from agreement instead of a fixed qualification. Carries its own `enabled`

enabled.description: Turn category routing on. Also gates the qualification scoring that runs when someone finishes training

fallback.description: What an annotator with no matching qualification is given

qualification.description: How training performance becomes a per-category qualification: `source` (training, prestudy or both), `threshold` (0-1, default 0.7) and `min_questions` (default 1)

system_prompt.description: Overrides what the chat assistant is told. Takes a `template` string, which may interpolate `task_name`, `task_description`, `annotation_labels`, `instance_text` and `instance_id`. The default carries all of those and instructs the model not to name a label

codebook.description: The shared label set a scheme opts into with a scheme-level `codebook: true`, edited from /codebook and stored per project

distiller.description: What the distilled, prompt-facing view of the codebook contains: include, include_types, include_doc_sections, scope, procedure, max_chars

enabled.description: Force the codebook on or off. Left unset it turns itself on when a scheme sets `codebook: true`, or under qda_mode/solo_mode

mode.description: Who may change codes: fixed, extensible (annotators may add) or open (annotators may add and edit)

codebook_invivo_key.description: Key that opens the in-vivo 'code from selection' composer while text is selected in a codebook-backed span scheme. Only the first character is used

codebook_mode.description: Top-level shorthand for codebook.mode, and the value that wins when both are set. Unset it resolves to open under qda_mode/solo_mode and fixed otherwise; a crowdsourcing backend force-locks fixed

completion_code.description: Code shown when an annotator finishes, for crowdsourcing payout

config_file.description: Path to the config file being run. Written by the loader from the command line, not something to set yourself; task_dir falls back to its directory

corpus_map.description: Multi-document corpus map: embed, cluster, project with UMAP and build a KNN graph, then give annotators a 2D navigation surface at /corpus. The heavy compute is lazy and never runs at boot

build_on_start.description: Build the map as soon as items load, rather than on first request

cluster_labeling.description: How clusters get their human-readable names

cot_segmentation.description: Split a long chain-of-thought string into labelable steps once, at load time, so the cot_trace display and the process_reward scheme read the same cached list

llm_max_chars.description: Characters of reasoning sent to the model under the llm strategy

markers.description: Separator strings for the markers strategy

max_steps.description: Hard cap on steps per item, which keeps pathological input from reaching the UI

min_step_chars.description: Steps shorter than this are merged into the previous one

sentences_per_step.description: Sentences grouped into one step by the sentence strategy

source_key.description: Item field holding the reasoning string. Required whenever the block is present

strategy.description: How to split: blank_line, numbered, markers, sentence, llm, or auto. llm needs an ai_support or judge_alignment endpoint and falls back to the heuristics if it cannot reach one

target_key.description: Item field the step list is written to. Point the display's and scheme's `steps_key` at this

credentials.description: How credentials in the config are resolved before use

env_file.description: Path to a .env file loaded before substitution

env_substitution.description: Expand ${VAR} references in config values from the environment

crowdsourcing.description: Crowd platform integration (Prolific, MTurk and others)

curation.description: Semantic curation (the Catalog): an embedding index over items, similarity search, and saved slices that stay live as data arrives

embed_on_ingest.description: Embed each item as it arrives. Off by default because it adds boot time and memory

text_key.description: Item field to embed. Empty means the item's text field

customjs_hostname.description: Hostname custom JavaScript is served from

ttl_seconds.description: How long a cached fetch stays fresh

data_directory.description: Load every data file in a directory instead of listing them

data_directory_encoding.description: Text encoding used to read files under data_directory

data_files.description: Data files, relative to task_dir. Each entry is either a path string or a mapping carrying per-file overrides (see flask_server.py:493).

database.description: Database connection for item or user storage

dataset_metadata.description: Descriptive metadata for the generated dataset card and Zenodo deposit: license, authors, citation, keywords, version, funding, related_links, tags, task_categories. Title and description fall back to the task's own name and description

datasets.description: Versioned evaluation datasets and experiment runs, served at /datasets

storage.description: Where datasets are stored: file or sqlite. Anything else falls back to file

debug.description: Run in debug mode. This disables admin authentication and skips login entirely, so it must never be set on a deployed server

debug_log.description: Which halves of the debug logging to turn on: all, ui, server or none. The --debug-log flag writes this key

debug_phase.description: Jump straight to a workflow phase, for UI debugging

diversity_ordering.description: Embed and cluster the corpus, then serve items round-robin across clusters so an annotator sees the range of the data early

auto_clusters.description: Pick the cluster count from the corpus size instead of num_clusters

enabled.description: Turn diversity ordering on. assignment_strategy: diversity_clustering turns it on regardless

items_per_cluster.description: Target items per cluster used to size an automatic k

model_name.description: Sentence-transformer model used for the embeddings

num_clusters.description: Clusters to build, when auto_clusters is off

prefill_count.description: How many items are ordered ahead of the annotator

preserve_visited.description: Keep an item in its place in the order once it has been seen

recluster_threshold.description: Fractional corpus growth that triggers a recluster

trigger_ai_prefetch.description: Warm AI suggestions for the items about to be served

embedding_visualization.description: 2D embedding scatter of the corpus on the admin dashboard, coloured by label

image_embedding_model.description: Image embedding model, for image tasks

include_all_annotated.description: Always include annotated items, on top of the sample

label_source.description: Which label colours the points: mace or majority

embeddings.description: The project-wide embedder shared by the corpus map, diversity ordering and duplicate detection. `backend` (auto by default), plus `model`, `source_field`, `cache_dir`, `media_root`; anything else is passed through to the backend. A custom backend needs `entrypoint` ('module.path:callable') or `endpoint` (an HTTP URL)

event_template.description: Cross-document event registry: admin-defined slots that annotators fill with evidence drawn from many documents

allow_annotator_create.description: Let annotators create new events, not only fill existing ones

name.description: Name of the template, shown in the UI

seed_events.description: Events to pre-create when the registry is first written. Either the events themselves or a path to a JSON file of them. Seeding is id-idempotent, so an existing event is never clobbered

export_annotation_format.description: Formats the periodic auto-export writes, as a list (a bare string is accepted). Empty means no auto-export

export_include_annotation_changes.description: Write annotation_changes.csv, the timestamped record of every answer revision. Off by default: it is far larger than the annotations and carries interaction detail not every study wants to distribute

export_include_phase_data.description: Include consent, instruction and survey responses in exports. Off by default: survey answers are usually where the PII is

format_handling.description: How rich text and markup in item fields are rendered

gold_standards.description: Items with known labels, used to score annotators

accuracy.description: Accuracy an annotator must hold to keep going. A bare fraction, or a mapping with `min_threshold` and `evaluation_count`

auto_promote.description: Promote annotators who pass to the full task. A flag, or a mapping with `min_annotators` and `agreement_threshold`

feedback.description: What an annotator is told after a gold item. A mapping with `show_correct_answer` and `show_explanation`; both off means silent scoring

frequency.description: Insert a gold item every N items

geometry_iou_tolerance.description: Overlap a drawn answer must reach to count as correct, as a fraction

gold_standards_file.description: Gold items file, the flat alternative to the gold_standards block

header_file.description: Ignored. The header template path is no longer configurable, and nothing reads this key -- `potato validate` reports it

header_logo.description: Logo image shown in the header

highlight_linebreaks.description: Make line breaks visible in item text

horizontal_key_bindings.description: Lay keyboard shortcut hints out horizontally

host.description: Interface to bind. 0.0.0.0 exposes the server beyond localhost

huggingface_backup.description: Mirror the annotation directory to a Hugging Face dataset repo on a schedule. Needs `enabled` and `repo_id`; the token comes from `token` (env substitution is applied) or HF_TOKEN, and `schedule_minutes` sets the cadence. A misconfiguration logs an error and lets the server run

ibws_config.description: Iterative best-worst scaling: re-generates tuples each round, concentrating comparisons where the ranking is still uncertain

max_rounds.description: Rounds before the process stops, or null to run until every bucket is terminal

scoring_method.description: Estimator used to turn comparisons into scores

tuples_per_item_per_round.description: How often each item is compared in one round

icl_labeling.description: In-context-learning labeler that builds few-shot prompts from high-confidence annotations already collected. Configured in four nested blocks, not as flat keys

llm_labeling.description: When and how much the model labels

verification.description: Blind human checking of the model's labels

instance_display.$comment: Display types accepting span annotation targets: audio_dialogue, code, coding_trace, dialogue, document, eval_trace, interactive_chat, multi_agent_discussion, text
instance_display.description: How each item is rendered. Omit for plain single-field text.

key.description: Field in the data file to render.

type.description: Display type, from the display registry.

oneOf.description: Agent trace display with step cards and type badges
Audio player display
Podcast / interview dialogue: speaker bubbles, per-turn audio playback, ratings, spans, cross-turn linking
Source code display with syntax highlighting
Coding agent trace display with diff rendering, terminal blocks, and file tree
Conversation tree with collapsible branching nodes
Long chain-of-thought trace: vertical step cards with a sticky progress rail for process-reward verification
Depth map with windowing, colormap and a metre readout
Dialogue/conversation turns, optionally threaded by reply-to with timestamps and per-turn metadata
Document display for DOCX, Markdown, and other formats
Three-pane agent trace eval: reasoning, function calls, and final answer side-by-side
Scrollable image gallery with captions
HTML content display (sanitized)
Image display with optional zoom
Interactive agent chat with post-interaction trace display
Live AI agent viewer with real-time screenshots, controls, and interaction
Live coding agent viewer with real-time streaming and intervention controls
Multi-agent discussion with agent legend, colors, addressees, and filtering
Side-by-side comparison display
PDF document display with PDF.js rendering
Spreadsheet/table display with row or cell annotation
Plain text content display
Video player display
Web agent trace viewer with screenshots, SVG overlays, and step navigation

instance_reclaim.description: Take assignments back from annotators who abandoned them so the items can go out again. `enabled` (false) and `timeout_hours` (24), plus optional `stale`, `manual`, `quality_control` and `prolific` sections each carrying `preserve_completed_annotations`

category_key.description: Field used by the category_based assignment strategy.

id_key.description: Field holding each item's unique id.

text_key.description: Field holding the text shown to annotators.

item_store.description: Where item payloads live. `backend` is memory (the default) or paged; paged writes to `path` -- .item_cache.sqlite under the output directory when unset -- and keeps `cache_size` items resident. An unknown backend warns and falls back to memory rather than refusing to start

cache_size.description: Items the paged backend keeps in memory

path.description: SQLite file the paged backend uses

judge_alignment.description: LLM-as-judge alignment: score items with a judge, compare against the humans, and track the agreement across prompt versions

ai_support.description: Endpoint the judge uses; falls back to the global ai_support block. Several evaluators read this same override

few_shot.description: Few-shot examples added to the judge prompt

inline.description: Show the judge's prediction beside the item while annotating. `enabled` turns it on; without `compute_on_demand` it only shows predictions an admin already ran

schemas.description: Per-scheme judge settings, keyed by scheme name. The keys present are also an allow-list: only radio, select and likert schemes named here get judged. Omit it to judge every categorical scheme

judge_calibration.description: Judge calibration: auto-label a sample with one or more judges, have humans re-label the same items blind, and report the agreement and calibration curve

fraction.description: Fraction of the corpus to label, as an alternative to max_items

human.description: The human side: num_raters (1) and how gold is formed (`gold`, single by default)

k_samples.description: Samples per item, used to measure the judge's own consistency

models.description: Judge models to run and compare

output.description: Where the report goes: `dir` (judge_calibration_output) and a `files` block naming the labels, JSON report and HTML report

sampling.description: How the calibration sample is drawn: strategy (random), stratify_by, sample_size (200), seed (42)

state_dir.description: Run state directory. Unset it is .judge_calibration under the output directory

keystroke_logging.description: Content-blind typing dynamics on free-text fields -- when someone pauses, revises or pastes, never which keys -- and the composed/transcribed/pasted detection built on them

classify_paste_source.description: Try to tell a paste from outside the page from one that only moved text within it

detection.description: Rule-based flags: `enabled`, `calibrate`, `on_external_insert` (allow, warn, block or flag) and `thresholds`. Thresholds are scored server-side and withheld from the browser, which would otherwise tell an annotator exactly how slowly to paste to stay under the flag

disclose_to_annotators.description: Show the recording notice. Turning it off collects typing dynamics silently, which your consent documents and ethics approval have to cover

disclosure_text.description: Replace the default notice. Must be non-empty; omit it to keep the default

enabled.description: Record typing dynamics. Off by default: it records how annotators produce free text, so it is opt-in rather than something a project acquires by upgrading Potato

fidelity.description: How much is kept: off, summary (per-response statistics only), or events (raw streams as well)

flush_interval_ms.description: How often the browser posts its buffered events

idle_session_ms.description: Gap that ends one typing session and starts the next

include_schemas.description: Schemes to record. Empty means every free-text field

pause_thresholds_ms.description: Pause buckets the summary counts against. Must be positive integers

store_events.description: Write raw event streams to the typing store. Does nothing at summary fidelity, which the loader warns about

keyword_highlights_file.description: File of keywords to highlight in item text. A CSV or TSV with a `keyword` header column (plus optional label, schema, color) is the documented form; one keyword per line, and JSON/JSONL/YAML holding a keyword list, an object list or a {keyword: label} map, are read too. A `*` in a keyword matches any run of word characters. See docs/administration/productivity.md

layout.description: How the annotation questions are arranged on the page: a grid, collapsible groups, an explicit order, and responsive breakpoints. Without it every scheme stacks full-width in config order

breakpoints.description: Viewport widths, in pixels, where the grid reduces

grid.description: Grid the question forms are laid out in

groups.description: Collapsible titled sections, each holding named schemes. The way to keep a long question list navigable

order.description: Scheme names in the order they should appear, overriding config order

styling.description: Colours, padding and alignment for groups and forms

list_as_text.description: How a list-valued field is laid out. Sub-keys: text_list_prefix_type (alphabet, number, bullet or none), horizontal, alternating_shading. `true` turns it on with the defaults

live_agent.description: Run a live agent inside the annotation page, so annotators judge a conversation as it happens rather than a recorded trace. Its presence enables the feature, and an instance_display field of type live_agent renders it

live_coding_agent.description: Same idea for a coding agent: runs the agent against a repository and streams its tool calls into a live_coding_agent display field

acknowledge_untrusted_code_execution.description: Required alongside sandbox_mode: trusted. Confirms you accept that annotator-editable tool calls, including arbitrary shell commands, run directly on this host as the Potato user

ai_config.description: Model settings passed to the backend (model name, endpoint, API key). Server-side only: a request cannot override it, because it carries credentials

backend_type.description: Which agent backend drives the session: ollama_tool_use, anthropic_tool_use, openai_tool_use, claude_sdk

container_cli.description: Container tool to drive: docker or podman. Rootless Podman needs no root daemon

container_runtime.description: Alternative container runtime, passed straight through as --runtime. Use runsc for gVisor (syscall interception in userspace) or kata for a hardware VM boundary. Unset uses the daemon default

max_turns.description: Stop the agent loop after this many turns

sandbox_cpus.description: CPU limit for the sandbox container

sandbox_image.description: Image the sandbox container runs. Point this at your own image to give the agent more tooling; pin a digest if you need reproducibility

sandbox_memory.description: Memory limit for the sandbox container, in Docker syntax

sandbox_mode.description: Boundary the agent's tool calls run inside: container (Docker or Podman), bubblewrap (Linux hosts without a container runtime), or trusted (no isolation, requires acknowledge_untrusted_code_execution). The former docker, worktree and direct modes are deprecated aliases; worktree never provided isolation

sandbox_network.description: Container network mode. Left at none the agent cannot reach the network, so it cannot exfiltrate what it reads

sandbox_pids_limit.description: Maximum processes inside the sandbox container, which caps fork bombs

sandbox_root.description: Directory holding per-session workspace copies. Defaults to a .potato-sandboxes directory beside working_dir

sandbox_user.description: uid:gid the sandboxed tools run as. Defaults to nobody

system_prompt.description: Extra system prompt prepended to the agent's instructions

working_dir.description: Repository the agent works on. Copied per session into a sandbox workspace rather than used in place, so agent edits never touch it

login.description: Login mode. type: password, url_direct, or none

url_argument.description: Query parameter carrying the user id under url_direct login

mace.description: MACE competence estimation: infers per-annotator reliability and a predicted label per item from the disagreement pattern alone

min_annotations_per_item.description: Items with fewer annotators than this are left out of the fit

min_items.description: Refuse to fit until this many eligible items exist

num_restarts.description: EM restarts; the best-scoring run is kept

trigger_every_n.description: Refit after this many new annotations

max_annotations_per_item.description: Cap on how many annotators may label one item. -1 means unlimited

max_annotations_per_user.description: Cap on how many dataset items one annotator may receive. Left unset, the cap is the number of items loaded, so every annotator is offered the whole corpus; -1 is explicit unlimited, which is what a dynamic data source needs for items added after boot to be assignable. Injected attention checks and gold items do not count against it

max_session_seconds.description: Hard limit on one annotation session

mcp.description: Model Context Protocol control surface, letting an agent query and control this running task. Off unless every tool is named explicitly

allow_debug.description: Permit the MCP surface on a debug server. Off by default: debug disables admin authentication server-wide, so the two together are a remote shell

audit_log.description: File recording every MCP call and refusal, one JSON object per line

auth.description: Where per-agent tokens live. `tokens_file` defaults to mcp_tokens.json under task_dir

destructive.description: Second, separate opt-in for tools that discard work. A destructive tool must appear here and in mcp.tools, and callers must pass confirm: true

enabled.description: Register the /api/mcp/* endpoints. Without this they do not exist

scope.description: Limits on what agents may touch, e.g. `users` to restrict which annotators they can act on

tools.description: Allowlist of tool names an agent may call. Empty grants nothing, and an unrecognized name fails at startup rather than warning

media_directory.description: Directory served at /media/, so data files can reference local images, audio and video by relative path instead of an external URL

min_annotators_per_instance.description: Floor on annotators per item before it counts as done

mturk.description: Amazon Mechanical Turk. Needs `enabled: true` and `config_file_path` pointing at the credentials YAML, plus boto3 installed. MTurk closed to new customers in July 2026 and the loader says so on startup

num_annotators_per_item.description: Target annotators per item. Either a plain count or a mapping carrying `default` plus overlap-sampling and adaptive-boost rules

output_annotation_format.description: Deprecated, and read as `export_annotation_format` at load time with a warning (`json` becomes `jsonl`, since no exporter is called `json`). It will stop being read in a later release, so rename it. Annotations are stored as `<output_annotation_dir>/<user>/user_state.json` whatever it says; this key never changed that

partial_loading.description: Load items lazily rather than reading every file at startup

per_annotator_quota.description: Per-annotator workload caps: `default`, plus `by_user` and `by_user_role` overrides. Any other sub-key is rejected at load rather than ignored

persist_sessions.description: Keep annotator sessions across a server restart

phases.description: Per-phase configuration (consent, instructions, training, annotation, post-study). Either a list of phase objects or a mapping with an `order` key. Phase-level annotation_schemes replace the top-level list rather than adding to it

pocket.description: Pocket Mode: the phone-sized annotation surface at /pocket, served as a PWA with an offline queue

auto_redirect.description: Send phones and tablets that open /annotate to /pocket, when every scheme in the task is touch-capable. `?desktop=1` opts back out

batch_size.description: Items per batch request, which is also the offline queue depth. Clamped to 1-200

port.description: Port to listen on. The -p flag overrides this

pre_annotation.description: Seed annotations to show as a starting point for each item

prestudy.description: Legacy pre-study screening block. The only code that reads it is an unreferenced method, so it has no effect -- configure the screening phase through `phases` or `surveyflow` with `type: prestudy`

psychometrics.description: Live IRT. Fits item difficulty and annotator ability as labels arrive, so labels carry error bars and confident items can stop early

confidence_threshold.description: Posterior probability at which an item counts as resolved. Outside 0.5-1.0 it is ignored and 0.95 used

cost_per_judgment.description: Cost of one judgment, used to price the saved judgments on the dashboard

discrimination_flag_threshold.description: Items whose ability-versus-correctness correlation falls below this are flagged as likely codebook bugs

enabled.description: Fit the model and serve the dashboard. Adaptive routing additionally needs assignment_strategy: psychometric

min_annotators_per_item.description: Floor before an item may be stopped early, however confident the posterior

min_observations.description: Cold-start gate: routing falls back to random until this many labels exist, so early assignments build the overlap the model needs

refit_interval.description: Refit once this many new labels have arrived since the last fit

schema.description: Scheme the model scores. Defaults to the first radio or likert scheme

publish.description: Dataset publishing options: `default_target` (archive, huggingface or zenodo) and an `options` block covering which splits are included, aggregation, min_annotators, PII scrubbing, media bundling and file format. Publishing works with none of this set

qda_mode.description: Qualitative data analysis mode. Turning it on moves the defaults for memos, the codebook and case grouping together, rather than each being switched on separately

codebook.description: QDA codebook defaults: `enabled` (true) and `mode` (open). Sub-keys of qda_mode are not recursed into, so an unrecognized block is carried through for forward compatibility -- and a typo passes silently

memos.description: QDA memo defaults: `enabled` and `show_sidebar_by_default`, both true. Memo storage itself is universal; this block only sets the QDA defaults

random_seed.description: Seed for assignment shuffling, so an ordering can be reproduced

rbac.description: Role assignments and SSO role mapping

require_fully_annotated.description: Refuse to advance until every scheme on the page has an answer

require_no_password.description: Accept a username with no password

review_mode.description: Hotkey review queue. Once the current item is complete the page moves on by itself, which turns keyboard-labelled schemes into press-key-and-advance

advance_on.description: What counts as complete: `complete` (every scheme on the page has a value) or `required` (the required-validated ones do)

auto_advance.description: Advance without being asked. Set false to keep review mode on but navigate by hand

review_workflow.description: Reviewer routing and the kanban board at /admin/review. Keeps its own state per instance (pending, in_review, needs_second, adjudication, done) alongside the annotations

auto_enroll.description: Enroll every loaded instance at startup. Set false to enroll by hand

reviewers.description: Reviewer pool that round-robin rules draw from

routing.description: First-match rules of `when` (the shared condition grammar) plus `state`, `priority`, and either `assign_to` or `round_robin`

rooms.description: Multiplayer rooms at /rooms: live norming sessions, adjudication huddles and shadowing over a shared event log

max_members.description: Members allowed in one room. Clamped to 2-100

persist_votes.description: Write a room's final vote into each member's own annotations

poll_interval_ms.description: How often clients poll for room events. Clamped to 500-30000

schema.description: Scheme members vote on. Defaults to the first radio or likert scheme; with neither present, rooms disable themselves

who_can_create.description: Who may open a room: any member, or admin only

scheme_sets.description: Named, reusable lists of annotation schemes. A batch_assignment group names one in its `schemes` key to give that cohort its own questions

search.description: Full-text search over loaded items, backed by SQLite FTS5. Admin search is read-only and always available; annotator search-and-claim is a separate opt-in

annotator_claim.description: Let annotators search the corpus and claim their own next item. Refused at startup when combined with a sampling-dependent assignment strategy or an overlap cap, since self-selection breaks both. Allowed unconditionally under qda_mode/solo_mode

backend.description: Index backend. fts5 is the only one built in; any other name disables search with a warning

enabled.description: Build the search index at startup

max_instances.description: Ceiling on how many instances are indexed

secret_key.description: Flask session signing key. Set this for any deployment that must keep sessions valid across restarts

server.description: Nested port/host/debug block, an alternative to the top-level keys

server_debug.description: Backend debug logging. Note that only the phase pages (consent, instructions, surveys) read this key; the annotation page asks the logging module, which is driven by debug_log/verbose/debug

session_lifetime_days.description: Days before a persisted session expires

session_timeout_minutes.description: How long a signed-in session may sit idle before the server clears it. The clock restarts on every request, so it bounds inactivity, not the length of a shift

sessions.description: Group items into sessions by session_id or thread_id and score the whole session at /sessions. Schemes opt in with `session_level: true`

attributes.description: Item fields lifted onto the session

key.description: Item field holding the session id. Unset, detection tries session_id then thread_id, looking inside `metadata` as well as at the top level

site_dir.description: Directory holding the HTML templates for this task

site_file.description: Specific template file to render the annotation page with

solo_mode.description: Single-coder loop. An LLM labels the corpus, you review where it is least sure, and the prompt is refined from your corrections

batches.description: Batch sizes for LLM labeling: llm_labeling_batch (50) and max_parallel_labels (200)

confidence_routing.description: Where an item goes by confidence band: auto-accept, review, or human

edge_case_rules.description: Rules distilled from your corrections and applied before the model

embedding.description: Embedder for diversity and textbox similarity; `model_name` defaults to all-MiniLM-L6-v2

instance_selection.description: Weights that decide what you are shown next: low_confidence_weight (0.4), diversity_weight (0.3), random_weight (0.2), disagreement_weight (0.1), and the opt-in edge_case_rule, cartography and llm_predicted weights

labeling_functions.description: Programmatic labeling functions run alongside the model

labeling_models.description: Endpoints that label the corpus. Each is endpoint_type plus model, and optionally api_key, base_url, max_tokens, temperature, think, timeout

prompt_optimization.description: Automatic prompt search: enabled (true), find_smallest_model, target_accuracy (0.85), optimization_interval_seconds, and the accuracy/length/consistency weights

refinement_loop.description: The automatic refine-evaluate-keep cycle over the labeling prompt

revision_models.description: Endpoints used to revise the prompt. Defaults to labeling_models

thresholds.description: The stopping and agreement thresholds -- including end_human_annotation_agreement (0.90) and minimum_validation_sample (50) -- plus the per-scheme-type match tolerances

uncertainty.description: How model uncertainty is estimated: `strategy` (direct_confidence, direct_uncertainty, token_entropy, sampling_diversity) and a `sampling_diversity` block

surveyflow.description: Survey pages shown before and after annotation

task_description.description: Short description of the task, shown to annotators

task_dir.description: Working directory for all relative paths. Paths resolving outside it are rejected by validate_path_security().

task_layout.description: Custom HTML for the annotation form area

thinkaloud.description: Think-aloud mode: local speech-to-text over spoken rationales, plus rule-based detection of spoken label phrases

chunk_seconds.description: Recorder restart interval. Each chunk is a complete audio file so it can be decoded on its own. Clamped to 2-30

fillers.description: Filler lexicon behind the hesitation signal

model.description: Whisper model size for the faster_whisper backend

require_spoken_label.description: Nudge on Next when no label was committed by voice

schema.description: Scheme whose labels may be committed by voice. Defaults to the first radio scheme

stems.description: Override the accepted label-phrase stem patterns

stt.description: Speech-to-text backend: faster_whisper (local), mock (tests), or auto

allow_unauthenticated.description: Accept trace posts with no api_key set. Off by default: without it the webhook endpoints reject every request rather than running open

api_key.description: Shared secret for the trace webhooks, accepted as either Authorization: Bearer or X-API-Key

notify_annotators.description: Push newly ingested traces to connected annotators

training.description: Qualification phase annotators must pass before real items

triage.description: Rank items by a priority signal so failures, thumbs-down feedback and low scores get annotated first. Scoring runs as items are added, so it covers traces ingested at runtime as well as loaded files

default_priority.description: Priority given to items no rule matched

invert_signal.description: Negate signal_field, for scores where lower is worse

order.description: Queue direction: desc serves the highest priority first

rules.description: Rules of `when` (the shared condition grammar) plus priority and an optional badge; the highest-priority match wins. Leaving both this and signal_field unset installs built-in rules for errored agents, thumbs-down feedback and scores below 0.5

show_badge.description: Show the matching rule's badge on the item

signal_field.description: Item field read as a numeric priority when no rule matches

truth_serum.description: Surprisingly-popular scoring. Each annotator also predicts how many others will pick the same label, and an answer that beats its own predicted popularity wins over the majority

min_annotators.description: Predictions needed on an item before a surprisingly-popular verdict is computed. Values below 2 are raised to 2

question.description: Prompt shown above the prediction slider
examples: What percentage of other annotators will choose the same label as you?

schema.description: Scheme whose labels get popularity predictions. Defaults to the first radio scheme; with none, predictions stay inactive

ui_debug.description: Print browser-side debug logging to the console

iaa_drift_approx.description: Marks a codebook revision whose date was inferred rather than recorded

iaa_drift_baseline.description: Row label for the whole-project agreement figure

iaa_drift_below_baseline.description: Phrase following the percentage in the re-calibration prompt

iaa_drift_codebook_changes.description: Label preceding the list of codebook revisions on the timeline

iaa_drift_note.description: Sentence explaining what a window is and how it is scored

iaa_drift_recalibrate.description: Label on the prompt raised when agreement falls below baseline

iaa_drift_sparse.description: Note on a window holding too few items to judge

iaa_drift_th_window.description: Short column prefix for a window, e.g. the W in W1, W2

iaa_drift_title.description: Heading of the agreement-over-time section on /admin/iaa

iaa_drift_untimed.description: Note about items with no timestamp, which cannot be placed on the timeline

allow_all_users.description: Let anyone register and annotate, rather than only listed users

users.description: Allowlist of usernames, used when allow_all_users is false

verbose.description: Raise the log level. --verbose writes this key

very_verbose.description: Raise the log level further; equivalent to debug for logging purposes, without debug's effect on authentication. --veryVerbose writes this key

watch_data_directory.description: Rescan data_directory while the server runs and pick up new files

watch_poll_interval.description: Seconds between rescans when watch_data_directory is on

webhooks.description: Post task events to external URLs as they happen

endpoints.description: Endpoints to post to, and which events each one wants

title: Potato task configuration
